Universal Corp positions itself as a leading global leaf tobacco supplier with over 100 years of experience and presence across 30+ countries in all major growing regions, emphasizing its ability to commercialize the entire tobacco plant and supply all major varieties. The company operates across seven primary geographies spanning Africa, Brazil, the United States, South America, Central America, Europe, and Asia, relying on supply chains that extend to more than 25 countries.

Universal Corp disclosed a material weakness in internal control over financial reporting in its 10-K filing for fiscal year 2025. This control deficiency renders disclosure controls and internal controls over financial reporting ineffective. As a consequence, the company cannot use Form S-3 registration statements for capital-raising activities, restricting its access to efficient equity or debt financing channels. The company also recorded $10.6 million in restructuring and impairment costs during fiscal 2025 related to consolidation of European tobacco sheet operations. These developments emerge alongside planned initiatives including completion of a major expansion at the Lancaster, Pennsylvania facility and ongoing investments in the Universal Ingredients platform.

The business carries significant customer concentration risk, with sales to the top five customers exceeding 50% of consolidated revenues for each of the past three fiscal years. Imperial Brands plc and Philip Morris International, Inc., including their respective affiliates, each accounted for at least 10% of revenues in the fiscal year ended March 31, 2025. Beyond customer concentration, Universal Corp faces exposure to commodity price volatility, seasonal labor dependencies in rural communities, weather and climate impacts on crop yields, and the competitive pressure from thousands of companies in plant-based ingredients alongside smaller leaf tobacco suppliers and major customers who source directly from farmers. The company acknowledges higher overhead costs and pricing compared to smaller competitors, and operates amid complex global regulatory and political uncertainties across its geographically dispersed footprint.

Capital expenditures are planned in the $45 million to $55 million range, with initiatives centered on completing the Lancaster expansion, consolidating European tobacco sheet operations, growing the Universal Ingredients platform, and completing a pension de-risking transaction.

### BCC [Critical]
_[View on SEC](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1328581/000132858126000006/bcc-20251231.htm)_

_Triggers: regulatory action: Oregon Department of Environmental Quality, EPA._

Boise Cascade Co operates two complementary segments serving the North American building materials market. The Building Materials Distribution (BMD) segment runs a nationwide network distributing oriented strand board, plywood, lumber, siding, composite decking, doors, millwork, metal products, roofing, insulation, and engineered wood products. The Wood Products segment manufactures laminated veneer lumber, I-joists, laminated beams, structural and appearance-grade plywood, and ponderosa pine lumber. The company derives substantially all revenue from the United States, with secondary exposure to Canada. It competes against a broad field including national distributors BlueLinx Holdings and Georgia-Pacific, major plywood and OSB producers like Weyerhaeuser and Louisiana-Pacific, specialty competitors, and foreign imports principally from South America.

The company faces mounting environmental compliance obligations that will require capital deployment and operational adjustments. The EPA finalized a rule in February 2024 lowering the National Ambient Air Quality Standard for fine particulate matter, expanding non-attainment areas where facilities must meet more stringent emission limits and permitting requirements. The Medford, Oregon plywood mill was selected into the Oregon Department of Environmental Quality's Cleaner Air Oregon program in October 2024, triggering evaluation and potential mitigation expenses. The Elgin plywood mill must comply with EPA Regional Haze Rule requirements by March 31, 2026, following boiler control installation that began in May 2023. Additionally, the EPA published a Risk and Technology Review for Plywood and Composite Wood Products MACT standards in 2024; while concluding additional controls are not required, certain remanded sources remain unresolved, with a court-ordered deadline for revised rules in June 2026.

Boise Cascade's structural position carries significant customer concentration risk. Builders FirstSource and Home Depot represent its largest customers, with substantially all Builders FirstSource sales recorded in BMD. Within the Wood Products segment, BMD itself is the largest customer, representing approximately 71% of overall segment sales in 2025—comprising roughly 75% of EWP sales volumes and 51% of plywood sales volumes. This internal concentration limits pricing flexibility. The company also depends on wood fiber sourcing from Canada and South America, exposing it to commodity price volatility and foreign exchange fluctuations. It states disadvantages including exposure to wood fiber availability and cost fluctuations, OSB and veneer input cost volatility, customer consolidation pressure on margins, and competition from lower-cost manufacturers and foreign competitors.

Capital spending is planned at $160 million (range $150–170 million). The company completed a greenfield distribution center in Hondo, Texas in August 2025 and finished the Oakdale, Louisiana mill modernization in 2025. The Thorsby, Alabama I-joist production capability is substantially complete and will be operational in the first half of 2026. In December 2025, Boise Cascade acquired Holden Humphrey in Massachusetts for $33.4 million. The company is also developing veneer laminated timber products for mass timber applications.

### CTS [Critical]
_[View on SEC](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/26058/000119312526067039/cts-20251231.htm)_

_Triggers: regulatory action: U.S. Environmental Protection Agency._

CTS Corp is a global manufacturer of sensors, connectivity components, and actuators serving aerospace and defense, industrial, medical, and transportation markets. The company organizes its offerings into three product categories: Sense (controls, pedals, piezo sensing products, sensors, switches, transducers), Connect (EMI/RFI filters, capacitors, frequency control products, resistors, RF filters), and Move (piezo microactuators, rotary actuators). CTS positions itself as a leading provider of sensing and motion devices with custom engineered products designed for specific OEM applications. The company operates a global manufacturing footprint across North America, Europe, and Asia, with North America as its primary geography. It holds 285 patents worldwide and employs sales engineers focused on application-specific product design. CTS competes primarily on product features, technology, price, quality, reliability, and delivery speed.

The U.S. Environmental Protection Agency has initiated a potential settlement related to prior period costs, with discussions ongoing as of 2025. Beyond this pending settlement, CTS faces potential liability for environmental contamination at multiple sites, including National Priorities List (Superfund) sites. The magnitude and timing of any resolution remain unquantified in the filing. These environmental matters carry financial and operational implications that could extend across multiple periods.

CTS depends on a concentrated customer base, with Toyota Motor Corporation and Cummins, Inc. each representing approximately 10 percent of revenue. The company sources semiconductors, rare earth elements, conductive inks, and silver pastes from a limited number of suppliers, creating material supply chain vulnerability. Manufacturing and sourcing operations span geographically sensitive jurisdictions including China, Czech Republic, Mexico, Philippines, Poland, and Taiwan. Structurally, the company operates within cyclical industries and faces competition from both larger, more diversified domestic and foreign manufacturers. Customer consolidation has reduced the number of available suppliers, and customers retain the option to manufacture products themselves. Technological obsolescence represents an ongoing competitive risk.

In 2024, CTS completed an acquisition of SyQwest, LLC for $121.9 million. The company disclosed no specific capital expenditure plans or forward guidance for revenue or earnings in this filing. Disclosure controls and internal control over financial reporting remain effective.

### GTY [Critical]
_[View on SEC](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1052752/000119312526048965/gty-20251231.htm)_

_Triggers: litigation with disclosed exposure $150M+._

Getty Realty Corp is a net lease REIT that acquires, finances, and develops single-tenant retail properties across 44 states and Washington D.C. The portfolio concentrates on convenience stores, express tunnel car washes, automotive service centers (gasoline and repair, oil and maintenance, tire and battery, and collision), drive-thru quick service restaurants, and other freestanding retail. The company positions itself as internally managed with extensive acquisition and financing experience, emphasizing well-located properties that support automobility, portfolio diversification across property types and tenants, and an established presence in major metropolitan markets. The triple-net lease structure reduces operating expense exposure to Getty directly.

Getty faces material environmental litigation with a disclosed exposure of $150 million tied to the Lower Passaic River Superfund Site (Diamond Alkali). As a Potentially Responsible Party, Getty Properties Corp and 84 other settling parties agreed to pay a collective $150 million for remediation. A Modified Consent Decree was approved by the Court on December 18, 2024, though appeals from Nokia and Occidental remain pending before the Third Circuit Court of Appeals. Separately, Getty is named in MTBE contamination litigation filed by the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania (2014) and State of Maryland (2017), both alleging statewide contamination. The Pennsylvania case transferred to the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York as part of MTBE MDL proceedings, with initial discovery concluded and certain focus sites transferred to the Eastern District of Pennsylvania for trial. The Maryland case is in the U.S. District Court for the District of Maryland. Management has recorded accruals for both cases based on probable losses that are reasonably estimable, though specific amounts are not disclosed.

The company's competitive position carries meaningful structural constraints. Texas and New York together represent 32 percent of annualized base rent, creating significant geographic concentration. High dependence on petroleum marketing industry revenues creates sector-specific vulnerability. Tenant creditworthiness is difficult to assess due to lack of ratings, and the portfolio remains exposed to environmental contamination liabilities beyond current litigation. The illiquid nature of real estate investments limits portfolio flexibility, and the company depends on external capital sources for growth. In 2025, Getty purchased $273 million in assets and sold $18.3 million, continuing active portfolio turnover. The company issued $250 million in Series U Guaranteed Senior Notes due January 2036 and is redeveloping two properties as of December 31, 2025, with expansion initiatives focused on Houston, Memphis, Dallas, San Antonio, Las Vegas, and Atlanta.

### IPAR [Critical]
_[View on SEC](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/822663/000175392626000464/ipar-20251231.htm)_

_Triggers: material weakness in internal controls disclosed._

Interparfums operates as a producer and marketer of prestige fragrances, cosmetics, and related personal care products, primarily through license agreements with brand owners. The business splits into two segments: European operations, run through a 72%-owned Paris subsidiary, account for approximately 68% of net sales and focus on manufacturing in France; US operations generate 32% of sales and source components from the United States, Italy, China, Poland, and Turkey. The company distributes across more than 120 countries, with North America and Western Europe as primary markets. Interparfums positions itself as a nimble operator in the prestige fragrance space, citing its ability to work closely with brand partners due to company size, a successful track record of launches, and a strong portfolio of brands with devoted followings.

The company disclosed a material weakness in internal controls over financial reporting in this filing, indicating that disclosure controls and internal control over financial reporting are not effective. This represents a significant governance concern that undermines the reliability of financial and operational reporting. The weakness was not accompanied by a restatement or going concern language, but the failure of both disclosure controls and ICFR requires investor scrutiny of how management intends to remediate the control environment and when effectiveness will be restored.

The structural position reflects both geographic and operational dependencies that constrain flexibility. Macy's represents a material customer concentration at 10% of 2025 net sales, down from 12% in 2024. Manufacturing relies on third-party producers across multiple geographies, with limited control over these relationships. The company faces headwinds including reliance on license agreement renewals, substantially smaller financial resources than major competitors, exposure to foreign exchange fluctuations, seasonal weighting toward the second half of the year, and inflationary pressures on component costs. Recent impairments of the Rochas fashion trademark—$4 million in 2024 and $9.2 million cumulatively through 2022—signal challenges in asset valuations within the portfolio. The company acquired $19.7 million in assets from Amorepacific Europe in 2025 and completed purchase of the Off-White trademark in 2024.

Forward initiatives include expansion of the Solférino boutique to 50 additional doors in the first half of 2026, a Goutal Paris relaunch and new launches in 2027, Longchamp fragrance launch expected in 2027, Off-White fragrance launches beginning 2027, and a new David Beckham signature fragrance targeted by end of 2029.

### JBGS [Critical]
_[View on SEC](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1689796/000110465926016450/jbgs-20251231x10k.htm)_

_Triggers: litigation with disclosed exposure $185M+._

JBG SMITH Properties is a real estate owner and operator concentrated in the Washington D.C. metropolitan area, primarily National Landing, Crystal City, Pentagon City, Potomac Yard, and Northern Virginia, with secondary holdings in Tysons and Herndon. The company operates three business segments: Multifamily, encompassing 6,519 units (6,333 at company share) as of December 31, 2025; Commercial, with 7.3 million square feet of office, retail, and ground lease assets (6.9 million at company share); and Third-party Real Estate Services, a fee-generating business providing property management, asset management, development, leasing, and construction management services to external clients. The company positions itself on deep expertise in mixed-use urban infill, placemaking synergies across concentrated National Landing holdings, and development and value creation capabilities. It claims fastest-to-market build-to-suit capacity in its primary market and leverages scale from third-party services to drive market knowledge and buying power.

The Wardman Tower litigation presents material exposure. The Wardman Tower Residential Condominium Unit Owners Association filed suit in D.C. Superior Court seeking $185.0 million in compensatory damages plus treble damages under the D.C. Consumer Protection Procedures Act, alleging construction and design deficiencies and misrepresentations. Trial commenced November 10, 2025, and remains pending. Separately, the District of Columbia filed an antitrust lawsuit against RealPage, Inc., multifamily rental companies, and 14 owners/operators including JBG Associates, LLC (a company subsidiary), alleging unlawful coordination through use of RealPage revenue management systems and data sharing in violation of the D.C. Antitrust Act. That case is also pending.

The company carries structural vulnerabilities that compound execution risk. It discloses heavy geographic concentration in the Washington D.C. metropolitan area and National Landing; reliance on federal government spending and defense contractors; significant exposure to Amazon as a major tenant and investment driver; office assets experiencing lower demand due to work-from-home policies; and retail exposure to online and discount retailer competition. A U.S. federal government tenant exceeds the 10% threshold, creating tenant concentration risk. In 2025, the company took 202,926 square feet at 1901 South Bell Street out of service; in 2024, approximately 618,000 office square feet came out of service across multiple locations. The company recorded $65.8 million in impairment losses in 2025 (The Batley, 2200 Crystal Drive, development parcels, and wireless spectrum licenses) and $55.4 million in 2024 (1901 South Bell Street, 2101 L Street, 8001 Woodmont, and development parcels), signaling asset value deterioration.

In 2025, the company completed $61.2 million in acquisitions (Tysons Dulles Plaza and Dulles View), disposed of $654.0 million in assets (The Batley, WestEnd25, 8001 Woodmont, two development parcels, and a 40% interest in West Half venture), and acquired the remaining 45% interest in 1101 17th Street. Capital expenditures planned total $14.8 million. Key initiatives include completion of the 2011 Crystal Drive office amenity hub in the first half of 2026, stabilization of four recent multifamily deliveries (The Grace, Reva, Zoe, Valen), a 4.9 million square-foot National Landing placemaking development pipeline, and Crystal Drive Metro entrance and Long Bridge infrastructure projects.

### KALU [Critical]
_[View on SEC](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/811596/000119312526059575/kalu-20251231.htm)_

_Triggers: restatement of prior-period financials mentioned._

Kaiser Aluminum manufactures and sells semi-fabricated specialty aluminum mill products, including flat-rolled products, extruded products, drawn products, and cast aluminum products. The company serves four primary product categories: Aero/HS Products, Packaging, GE Products, and Automotive Extrusions. Operations are concentrated in North America as the primary geography, with secondary presence in Western Europe. Kaiser positions itself on leading positions in select end markets with high barriers to entry, supported by core metallurgical and process technology capabilities, long-standing relationships with blue-chip customers, and a broad product offering. The company markets highly engineered KaiserSelect® products with differentiated characteristics and maintains research and development centers backed by metallurgical expertise.

This filing contains a restatement of prior-period financials, which signals financial reporting adjustments that require investor review of the nature and magnitude of the corrections made.

Kaiser's structural position carries several material constraints. The company depends on a core group of significant customers, with the five largest accounting for 56% of net sales and the single largest customer representing 16% of revenue. Production is concentrated at Trentwood and Warrick facilities, creating vulnerability to operational interruptions. The company faces pricing pressure on many products with continued competitive pressure anticipated and has stated it is unable to pass fluctuations in energy, raw materials, operating supplies, and freight costs to customers. Downward pressure on pricing stems from customer cost-cutting initiatives. Kaiser competes against larger, better-capitalized rivals including Arconic Corporation, Constellium N.V., Novelis Inc., Tri-Arrows Aluminum, Norsk Hydro ASA, and foreign competitors with lower manufacturing costs. The company also faces substitution risk from alternative materials including glass, paper, flexible materials, plastic, titanium, composites, and carbon fiber, as well as steel manufacturers in automotive applications. Supply chain dependencies on South Africa, Europe, and China for heat treat plate present geographic exposure.

Kaiser has planned capex of $125 million (within a $120–130 million range) focused on Phase VII capacity expansion at Trentwood, commissioning of a fourth coating line at Warrick, modernization at Trentwood for thin gauge plate, and KaiserSelect quality enhancements for Aero/HS Products. A planned partial outage at Trentwood supports the capacity expansion project, and the Sherman, Texas soft alloy extrusion facility ceased operations.

### NXRT [Critical]
_[View on SEC](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1620393/000119312526077343/nxrt-20251231.htm)_

_Triggers: litigation with disclosed exposure $1.3B+._

NexPoint Residential Trust, Inc. operates as a multifamily residential real estate company focused on acquiring, owning, and operating apartment properties in the Southeastern and Southwestern United States. The company pursues a value-add strategy centered on Class B multifamily properties, employing capital improvements and active repositioning to create value. NexPoint positions itself around construction management and renovation expertise, leveraging the scale of its property manager, BH, which manages 92,000 multifamily units across markets. The company sources tenants primarily through direct multifamily apartment rentals, supplemented by ancillary revenue from utilities, late fees, pet fees, application fees, laundry, and cable TV services.

Two material lawsuits create substantial financial exposure. UBS Securities LLC is pursuing collection on $1.3 billion in judgments obtained against Highland-managed entities, with NexPoint implicated through its connection to James Dondero. Motions to dismiss were denied on March 26, 2025, and respondents are appealing; a status conference is scheduled for April 14, 2026. A separate bankruptcy trust lawsuit filed by Marc S. Kirschner against Dondero and others involves claims assigned to Hunter Mountain Investment Trust, with a status conference set for February 26, 2026. These litigations reflect ongoing disputes tied to Highland Capital Management's bankruptcy and create legal and financial uncertainty for the company.

NexPoint faces structural challenges that limit operational flexibility. Geographic concentration in the Southeast and Southwest increases exposure to regional downturns, while dependence on its external adviser and property manager creates operational risk. The company explicitly discloses that short-term leases expose it to rapid rent decline impacts and that substantial debt levels constrain financial flexibility and increase refinancing risk. Competition comes from well-capitalized institutional investors—insurance companies, private equity funds, sovereign wealth funds, pension funds, and other REITs—that can outbid on acquisitions. REIT qualification requirements further restrict the company's hedging and investment options, and the illiquidity of real estate limits its ability to adjust portfolio positioning quickly.

The company completed the $73.25 million acquisition of Sedona at Lone Mountain in Las Vegas in December 2025 and plans 12,984 interior rehabs. Capital expenditures are budgeted at $8.3 million, with a $200 million JPM revolving credit facility maturing in June 2028 supporting operations. Casualty events resulted in 22 units offline as of year-end 2025, with $167,000 in losses during the period.

### RNST [Critical]
_[View on SEC](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/715072/000071507226000017/rnst-20251231.htm)_

_Triggers: material weakness in internal controls disclosed._

Renasant Corp operates as a community bank holding company primarily across the Southeast through its Community Banks segment, which conducts substantially all business activities via 277 banking, lending and mortgage offices located throughout Louisiana, Mississippi, Alabama, Georgia and Florida, with a secondary presence in California, Illinois and Texas through Republic Business Credit. The company offers a comprehensive product suite spanning commercial and industrial loans, construction lending, real estate mortgages, consumer loans, specialty commercial lending including factoring and asset-based lending, SBA lending, equipment lease financing, healthcare specialty lending, deposit services, treasury management, and mortgage banking. Its Wealth Management segment, representing 2.4% of gross revenues in 2025, operates through a Trust division providing fiduciary and custodial services and a Financial Services division offering annuities, mutual funds and stocks through Park Place Capital. Renasant positions itself on a franchise model where local community bank presidents maintain autonomy while centralized functions achieve economies of scale and quality control, supported by 24-hour online and mobile banking.

Renasant disclosed a material weakness in internal controls over financial reporting, indicating the company's disclosure controls and internal control framework over financial reporting are not effective. This represents a significant governance concern requiring immediate attention to remediation efforts and heightened scrutiny of reported financials.

The company faces structural vulnerabilities stemming from its concentrated loan portfolio. Renasant self-discloses a high concentration of real estate-secured loans creating vulnerability to market decline, alongside significant commercial real estate concentration risk. Competitive positioning has intensified following 2023 bank failures, which heightened deposit competition. The company competes against a broad spectrum of larger regional and national banks, savings and loan associations, credit unions, finance companies, mortgage companies, brokerage firms, fintech companies and trust companies—many with greater resources and fewer regulatory constraints. Renasant's compliance costs remain elevated due to extensive banking regulation, a disadvantage versus less-regulated competitors.

During 2025, Renasant completed a merger with The First Bancshares, Inc. for approximately $7.6 billion, integrating 116 locations, and completed a core system conversion in August 2025. The company redeemed subordinated notes in October 2025 and authorized a $150 million stock repurchase program that same month. Renasant also divested substantially all assets of Southwest Georgia Insurance Services, Inc. on December 31, 2025, continuing a portfolio rationalization effort that included the July 2024 sale of Renasant Insurance, Inc.

### TDC [Critical]
_[View on SEC](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/816761/000162828026012671/tdc-20251231.htm)_

_Triggers: litigation with disclosed exposure $480M+._

Teradata Corp operates as a data analytics and AI platform company organized into two primary segments: Product Sales (encompassing recurring revenue from cloud and subscription offerings, perpetual software licenses, and hardware) and Consulting Services. The company's product portfolio spans recurring cloud subscriptions, perpetual licenses, and an expanding suite of AI capabilities including the Enterprise Vector Store, Teradata AI Factory, Enterprise Feature Store, ClearScape Analytics, and AgentBuilder. Teradata positions itself around autonomous AI operations and hybrid deployment flexibility, emphasizing massively parallel architecture with patented workload management across on-premises, AWS, Azure, Google Cloud, and private cloud environments. The company claims competitive advantage through four decades of domain expertise, best price-performance positioning, and an open ecosystem approach combining structured and unstructured data for enterprise AI use cases.

On February 19, 2026, Teradata entered into a settlement agreement with SAP SE, SAP America, Inc., and SAP Labs, LLC, resolving litigation with a gross payment to Teradata of $480 million. Net proceeds are estimated at $355–$362 million after transaction fees and expenses. This settlement represents a material one-time event with direct cash impact to the company.

The competitive landscape presents structural headwinds. Teradata faces well-capitalized competitors including AWS, Microsoft Azure, Google Cloud, Databricks, and Snowflake—companies with greater financial resources, widespread distribution, and established brand recognition. The company discloses long sales cycles with multiple approval levels, seasonal booking patterns (lower in Q1, higher in Q4), and shifting customer preferences toward cloud-only deployments. Supply chain concentration exists through Flex Ltd., which assembles and configures hardware components. Regulatory uncertainty around AI/ML capabilities and evolving compliance requirements, combined with dependency on cloud service provider relationships and their competing offerings, represent stated disadvantages. No single customer exceeds 10% of total revenue.

Key forward initiatives center on AI and cloud infrastructure: the Enterprise Vector Store, Teradata AI Factory with Nvidia NIM support, AgentBuilder for rapid AI deployment, MCP Server for enterprise data connectivity, and Autonomous Customer Intelligence capabilities. The company uses non-GAAP measures including Total Annual Recurring Revenue, Public Cloud ARR, Cloud Net Expansion Rate, and free cash flow. Disclosure controls and internal control over financial reporting are effective; no material weaknesses, restatements, or going concern language appear in the filing.

### TWO [Critical]
_[View on SEC](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1465740/000146574026000009/two-20251231.htm)_

_Triggers: litigation with disclosed exposure $375M+._

Two Harbors Investment Corp. is a mortgage REIT operating across three interconnected segments: mortgage servicing rights (MSR), agency residential mortgage-backed securities (RMBS), and mortgage servicing operations. Through its TH MSR Holdings subsidiary, the company owns and manages MSR assets approved by Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac, acquiring these through flow and bulk purchases and loan recapture. Its Agency RMBS segment invests in securities whose principal and interest are guaranteed by U.S. government agencies or GSEs, collateralized by fixed-rate, adjustable-rate, and hybrid mortgage loans. The company operates RoundPoint Mortgage Servicing LLC, which services loans underlying its MSR assets and third-party MSR, and also runs a direct-to-consumer mortgage originations platform. Two Harbors positions itself as an internally-managed REIT with core competencies in interest rate and prepayment risk management, leveraging MSR and Agency RMBS diversification to deliver stable performance across market conditions. The company operates exclusively in the United States.

Two Harbors paid $375 million in September 2025 to settle litigation with PRCM Advisers LLC, Pine River Capital Management L.P., and Pine River Domestic Management L.P., resolving all claims across federal and state court proceedings. All claims were dismissed with prejudice and Pine River relinquished ownership of intellectual property as part of the settlement. This represents a material cash outflow and eliminates an identified litigation exposure.

Two Harbors faces structural constraints that differentiate its competitive position. The company acknowledges that many competitors are substantially larger with greater resources, and that the Federal Reserve may compete through asset purchases. The business carries inherent leverage risk—leverage magnifies losses in adverse conditions—alongside challenges specific to mortgage servicing: illiquid assets that are difficult to finance and sell quickly, dependence on GSE viability and regulatory structure, complex and evolving regulatory environments that increase costs, and limited ability to hedge effectively under REIT tax rules. The company disclosed no customer or vendor concentrations in the extraction data.

Two Harbors announced a merger with United Wholesale Mortgage LLC (UWM) in 2025, expected to close in Q2 2026. RoundPoint obtained Ginnie Mae servicing approval in Q3 2025 and operates a direct-to-consumer originations platform launched in Q2 2024. No capex figures or forward earnings guidance were provided.

### UNFI [Critical]
_[View on SEC](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1020859/000102085925000054/unfi-20250802.htm)_

_Triggers: regulatory action: U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) Region VI._

United Natural Foods Inc operates as a wholesale distributor and retailer of grocery and specialty products across North America. The company comprises three segments: Natural, which distributes natural, organic, and specialty products alongside a portfolio of owned brands and snack manufacturing; Conventional, distributing conventional grocery items and owned brands; and Retail, operating 75 Cub Foods and Shoppers stores offering grocery, general merchandise, health and beauty, and pharmacy services. UNFI maintains a presence across all 50 U.S. states and ten Canadian provinces, positioning itself around a portfolio of 230,000 products delivered through 52 distribution centers spanning 30 million square feet. The company emphasizes heritage in natural and organic products and an expanding digital and professional services offering as competitive differentiation against traditional and specialty wholesalers, national chains, supercenters, club stores, and online retailers.

The EPA Region VI initiated enforcement action against UNFI following a December 2023 inspection, issuing a Notice of Potential Violation for Federal Clean Air Act Section 112(r) violations at a distribution center. A settlement proposal was issued August 4, 2025, with an expected penalty of $300,000. Separately, UNFI recorded a $24 million non-cash impairment charge on a distribution center in the East region during fiscal 2025, adding to $43 million in impairment charges recorded in fiscal 2024 affecting corporate offices, retail stores, and distribution facilities. These write-downs reflect ongoing restructuring of the distribution network and underperformance at certain locations.

UNFI faces structural headwinds from low margins endemic to grocery distribution and intensifying competition from well-resourced consolidating competitors, mass market players expanding natural and organic assortments, and retailers building direct relationships or self-distribution capabilities. The company disclosed that one Natural customer, including affiliated entities under common control, represented more than 10% of fiscal 2025 net sales, creating meaningful revenue concentration risk. Supplier concentration is more diffuse, with no single vendor exceeding 5% of purchases. The stated disadvantage list explicitly flags margin compression from inflation slowdown, loss of higher-margin demand in natural products during inflationary periods, and lower-cost structures deployed by clubs, outlets, and online channels as persistent competitive pressures.

UNFI is investing $250 million in capital expenditures focused on network optimization and automation. Key initiatives include full case automation deployment at the Manchester, Pennsylvania distribution center (completed Q3 fiscal 2025), development and launch of a 1 million square foot automated facility in Sarasota, Florida (operational Q4 fiscal 2025), lean daily management implementation across 28 distribution centers, and closure of the Allentown, Pennsylvania facility in early fiscal 2026. These efforts reflect a multi-year transformation of the distribution footprint toward higher-automation and efficiency.

### CABO [Notable]
_[View on SEC](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1632127/000163212726000005/cabo-20251231.htm)_

_Triggers: $497M impairment disclosed; 1 pending litigation matter(s) disclosed; 2 regulatory action(s) disclosed; CEO changed during fiscal year._

Cable One operates a single broadband communications business serving residential and business customers across 24 Western, Midwestern, and Southern states, with primary operations in Arizona, Idaho, Mississippi, Missouri, Oklahoma, South Carolina, and Texas. The company provides data, video, and voice services to both segments. Cable One positions itself around its fiber-based and HFC infrastructure, claiming gigabit and multi-gigabit download speeds available to all passings, network reliability with peak bandwidth utilization below 20%, and deep customer relationships built over 30 years in non-metropolitan markets. The company emphasizes low-cost operations and acquisition integration capability as competitive advantages.

Cable One took a $497.2 million non-cash impairment of indefinite-lived franchise agreements intangible assets in fiscal 2025, driven by stock price decline, reduced estimated future cash flows from increased competition, and an increased discount rate. An additional $88.8 million goodwill impairment was recorded. These write-downs reflect material pressure on the company's underlying business valuation. The company also experienced a CEO change during the fiscal year. On the regulatory front, the FCC's May 2024 Open Internet Order reclassifying broadband as a telecommunications service under Title II was overturned by the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Sixth Circuit in January 2025, returning broadband to information service status with limited FCC oversight. Separately, FCC rules adopted in November 2023 prohibiting differential broadband access based on income level, race, ethnicity, color, religion, or national origin remain under challenge in federal court. Cable One faces pending intellectual property litigation alleging infringement in network infrastructure, modem technology, and VoIP services across multiple named defendants, though the company does not view proceedings as material.

The competitive environment presents concrete structural headwinds. Cable One explicitly identifies declining residential video profitability due to rising programming and retransmission fees, customer cord-cutting, escalating content licensing costs, and competition from well-capitalized entrants and telephone companies. Over-the-top video providers including Netflix, Disney+, Amazon Prime Video, Apple TV+, HBO Max, Hulu, Paramount+, Peacock, YouTube TV, and Sling TV compete directly for video subscribers. Broader competitive pressure comes from telephone companies offering DSL or fiber-to-the-node service, municipalities and cooperatives with fiber networks, regional fiber providers, wireless internet providers including 5G and fixed wireless access (FWA) operators, and government-subsidized broadband deployments. The company also faces regulatory uncertainty regarding net neutrality and broadband pricing, plus potential franchise non-renewal or termination risks.

Near-term initiatives include DOCSIS 4.0 deployment across markets, multi-gigabit service rollout to remaining markets, a mobile service pilot with a virtual network enabler, and completion of a unified billing platform implementation in 2025. Cable One is acquiring remaining equity interests in MBI for $480 million, with closing scheduled for October 1, 2026, and is pending the sale of assets to Point Broadband Holdings, LLC. The company completed divestitures of Ziply, MetroNet, and a small equity investee in 2025.

### TALO [Notable]

Talos Energy is an upstream oil and gas exploration and production company operating primarily in the United States Gulf of America across deepwater, shelf, and Gulf Coast assets, with secondary operations in Mexico's Sureste Basin. The company produces crude oil, natural gas, and natural gas liquids. Talos positions itself on a high-quality, oil-weighted production base concentrated in high-margin deepwater assets, backed by decades of offshore operational expertise and proven seismic technology capabilities. The company faces competition from both large integrated oil and gas majors and independent exploration and production companies, but notes that competitors possess significantly greater financial resources and superior ability to respond to industry shifts.

The $454.5 million impairment of oil and natural gas properties in fiscal 2025 resulted from ceiling test evaluation driven by lower commodity prices and reduced proved reserves estimates. Concurrent with this write-down, the company executed leadership transitions, with Paul Goodfellow appointed President and Chief Executive Officer effective March 1, 2025, and a CFO change during the year. Three pending litigation matters also warrant attention: Equinor USA's suit against Talos ERT LLC over decommissioning and plugging expenses on Mississippi Canyon 941, with trial scheduled for 2026 or potentially extending into 2027; and two Parish-level suits against Stone Energy Corporation and co-defendants alleging Coastal Resources Management Act violations, with one trial set for October-November 2027. Financial exposure from the litigation remains unspecified in the filing.

The business carries material structural dependencies. Shell Trading (US) Company represented 35% of oil, natural gas, and NGL revenues for the year ended December 31, 2025, while Exxon Mobil Corporation and Chevron Corporation accounted for 23% and 12% respectively. This concentration creates meaningful revenue vulnerability. The company self-discloses that deepwater operations carry significantly higher operational and financial risks, that it maintains limited control over non-operated properties, and that it faces exposure to prolonged low commodity prices. Geographic concentration in a single region presents additional risk from regional disruptions. Operationally, recent facility events included a 52-day Helix Producer I dry-dock in 2024 for Coast Guard inspection, temporary shut-in of Genovesa due to subsurface safety valve failure in Q4 2025 (deferring approximately 3 MBoepd), and the successful drilling and completion of Cardona in late 2025 tied to the Pompano facility.

The company plans capital expenditures in the $500–550 million range for 2025, with key projects including first production from the CPN well in the second half of 2026, expansion of Katmai Field's Tarantula facility to 38 MBoepd, progression of the Monument Project multi-well development, a Daenerys appraisal well spud in Q2 2026, and return of Genovesa to production in Q3 2026. Recent M&A activity includes the 2024 completion of a $916 million acquisition of QuarterNorth Energy, divestitures to TotalEnergies E&P USA and Zamajal, and a pending 2026 divestiture to Zamajal.

NetScout positions itself around four decades of experience in service assurance, emphasizing comprehensive visibility across both data and control plane traffic, scalability to handle increasing network loads, and deep packet inspection technology deployable across multiple form factors.

In governance matters, the company replaced its CFO during the fiscal year. Current forward-looking initiatives include the Titan XT next-generation automated dispensing system launch, migration of the OmniSphere cloud platform from on-premise infrastructure, expansion of Central Pharmacy Dispensing and IV Compounding Services, enhancement of Specialty Pharmacy Services and 340B optimization offerings, and expansion of the EnlivenHealth platform into retail and community pharmacy segments. No specific capex guidance or revenue projections were disclosed.

### PHIN [Notable]

PHINIA INC. is a supplier of advanced fuel systems and aftermarket automotive components. Its Fuel Systems segment provides fuel injection systems, fuel delivery modules, electronic control modules, software, and original equipment service solutions for combustion and hybrid propulsion applications. The Aftermarket segment sells maintenance and diagnostic equipment, remanufactured products, and electrical components like starters and alternators to independent aftermarket customers and OEMs. The company operates globally across the United States, Europe, and Asia as primary markets, with secondary exposure to off-highway and industrial applications. PHINIA positions itself as a highly engineered supplier with a broad fuel injection portfolio, global reach to major OEMs, and proprietary intellectual property spanning over 2,750 patents and 1,900 trademarks worldwide.

German authorities are investigating alleged diesel defeat device violations involving engine control units, software, and calibration services that PHINIA supplied indirectly through its Delphi Technologies entity to light vehicle OEMs prior to 2020. The investigation began in 2022, and authorities have conducted facility searches; the matter remains ongoing with PHINIA cooperating. Separately, PHINIA settled a Tax Matters Agreement dispute with BorgWarner, its former parent, related to indirect tax obligations predating the spin-off. Under the settlement, PHINIA will pay a total of $78 million across multiple tranches through 2026, with BorgWarner having paid the company $7 million for pre-spin-off corporate income taxes. Additionally, the company recorded a $21 million non-cash impairment in 2024 related to property, plant, and equipment at a European Fuel Systems manufacturing facility.

PHINIA faces substantial customer concentration, with General Motors representing 18% of 2025 net sales and the top five customers accounting for 37% of total sales. The company competes against a large, well-capitalized field including Robert Bosch GmbH, Cummins Inc., Denso Corporation, Valeo, Hitachi Astemo, and others, many of which possess greater financial resources and more diversified product portfolios. Cost pressures are material: PHINIA cannot pass through 100% of commodity and tariff increases to customers, and customers are demanding annual price reductions while expanding global sourcing. The company also relies on fewer supply sources for certain components and faces exposure to volatile commodity prices and elevated inflation since 2024.

Planned capital expenditure for the forward period is $125.9 million. Key initiatives include the 2025 acquisition of Swedish Electromagnet Invest AB for $47 million to add natural gas and hydrogen ignition systems, a shift of the OES business to the Fuel Systems segment for distribution, and expansion efforts in the commercial vehicle and hybrid/plug-in hybrid electric vehicle markets.

RH operates as a luxury home furnishings retailer through three segments: its primary RH segment encompassing retail galleries, e-commerce, sourcebooks, trade services, and outlet locations; Waterworks, a luxury bathroom fixtures and furnishings business; and a real estate segment that is immaterial to current operations. The company sells furniture, lighting, textiles, bathware, décor, outdoor and garden products, and baby and child furnishings primarily in the United States and Canada, with secondary presence in Europe. RH positions itself as offering the most comprehensive collection of luxury home furnishings under a single brand, supported by architecturally distinctive galleries, an integrated omnichannel platform spanning retail, digital, and print channels, and proprietary product development capabilities. The company competes against regional and national home furnishings retailers, online-centric competitors, interior design trade specialists, antiques dealers, and mail-order catalogs—though it claims no direct competitor of comparable scale operates with its combined product offering, operational infrastructure, and brand positioning.

RH faces multiple pending litigation exposures across four categories: securities class action claims related to trading in company securities; wage and hour and employment practices cases seeking class certification; product liability and personal injury claims tied to products sold and gallery operations; and intellectual property infringement claims involving copyrights, trademarks, patents, and trade dress. Additionally, the Consumer Product Safety Commission initiated a product recall in fiscal 2025 that resulted in $1.913 million in costs and inventory charges. The company recorded $3.597 million in inventory and property impairments in fiscal 2025 related to galleries under construction, following larger impairments of $19 million and $17 million in fiscal 2024 tied to German galleries and construction-phase facilities. These charges signal execution challenges in international expansion.

RH's supply chain carries material concentration risk. Vietnam accounts for 39% of sourced products, China 13%, with Indonesia and India supplying the remainder of Asian sourcing. North America represents 21% of sourcing (13% from the United States), and Europe and other countries comprise 10%. On the vendor side, the top single vendor accounted for 14% of purchase dollar volume in fiscal 2025, while 76% of purchases came from just 28 vendors. The company acknowledges disadvantages including competitors with greater financial resources, price-based competitive pressure, high reliance on foreign manufacturing, and exposure to tariff and trade policy uncertainty.

RH has allocated $240 million to $260 million in capex (midpoint $250 million) and is advancing several initiatives: launching RH Estates in spring 2026 with RH Bespoke furniture offerings, opening RH Milan and RH London design galleries in 2026, constructing design compounds in Naples, Miami, and Walnut Creek, enhancing the World of RH digital platform in 2026, and planning an RH Sydney gallery for future opening. The company completed a $32 million acquisition in fiscal 2025 and opened the RH Paris gallery on the Champs-Élysées in September 2025, continuing its international gallery expansion strategy.

Gibraltar Industries operates across three business segments serving distinct end markets. The Residential segment is the largest, supplying roofing accessories, metal roofing, rain dispersion, ventilation, mail solutions, and outdoor living products through retail home centers, wholesalers, distributors, contractors, and online channels. The Agtech segment designs and manufactures controlled environmental agriculture facilities, custom greenhouses, and structural canopies for commercial growers, agricultural research, and retail applications. The Infrastructure segment provides expansion joints, structural bearings, rubber seals, and bridge cable protection systems for highway and airport projects. The company operates across the United States and Canada with manufacturing facilities in 23 states and Canada, positioning itself on broad product ranges, speed of service, direct customer relationships, recognized brands, and local production capabilities.

Gibraltar recorded a $176 million impairment in fiscal 2025 tied to the Renewables business, which the company subsequently divested for $70 million in 2026. This impairment reflects both held-for-sale classification and discontinued operations treatment. The company also recorded a $6 million intangible asset impairment in 2024 related to a rebranding initiative and trademark discontinuation in the Agtech segment. Offsetting these charges, Gibraltar executed substantial acquisition activity: the $1.335 billion acquisition of OmniMax International completed in 2026, along with $117 million for Lane Supply (structural canopies) and $106 million for three metal roofing manufacturers (2025). The OmniMax acquisition represents a material expansion of the Residential segment, while the metal roofing and Lane Supply deals target local market penetration and new customer verticals.

The company's competitive position carries several structural constraints. Its largest customer represents 12% of sales, creating customer concentration risk in the Residential segment where one home improvement retailer exceeds the 10% disclosure threshold. The market itself is fragmented and driven by contractor preferences, subjecting Gibraltar to price pressure despite its scale advantages. The company faces commodity price volatility in steel, aluminum, and glass, and exposure to residential construction cyclicality. The OmniMax acquisition has created substantial debt that management identifies as limiting financial flexibility. The company sources raw materials through a China office, introducing geographic supply chain dependencies. Competitors range from smaller regional players to larger, better-capitalized firms with established brand recognition, though Gibraltar's manufacturing footprint and direct customer access differentiate its positioning.

Integration of OmniMax dominates near-term strategy alongside execution of Agtech backlog and organic growth initiatives. The company is pursuing 80/20 lean initiatives and quote-to-cash process optimization. No capex targets or revenue guidance has been disclosed.

### ACAD [Notable]
_[View on SEC](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1070494/000119312526072519/acad-20251231.htm)_

_Triggers: 6 pending litigation matter(s) disclosed; 1 regulatory action(s) disclosed._

ACADIA PHARMACEUTICALS INC develops treatments for neurological diseases and rare diseases, anchored by two FDA-approved products. NUPLAZID (pimavanserin) treats Parkinson's disease psychosis and represents the first and only FDA-approved drug for PDP hallucinations and delusions; the company holds approximately 25% market share in this indication. DAYBUE (trofinetide) treats Rett syndrome and is similarly the first and only FDA-approved therapy for this rare disease, supported by Orphan Drug Designation and FDA Fast Track Status. The pipeline includes remlifanserin for Alzheimer's disease psychosis and Lewy Body Dementia psychosis, ACP-101 for Prader-Willi syndrome, and several earlier-stage candidates. The United States is the primary geography, with secondary presence in Europe, Canada, Israel, and Japan.

ACADIA faces material legal and regulatory headwinds on both products. In January 2026, the European Medicines Agency Committee for Medicinal Products for Human Use issued a negative trend vote on the marketing authorization application for trofinetide for Rett syndrome, prompting the company to request re-examination with CHMP opinion expected in February 2026. On the securities litigation front, a certified class action alleging failures to disclose statistical and design deficiencies in materials submitted for a pimavanserin supplemental new drug application for dementia-related psychosis has concluded discovery and completed pretrial motions briefing, with a pretrial hearing scheduled for April 10, 2026. Related opt-out litigation remains stayed pending the class action outcome. A derivative action alleging breach of fiduciary duty and insider trading reached settlement in principle in January 2026 with $1.5 million in attorneys fees to be paid by insurance. Three patent infringement cases involving NUPLAZID are pending or on appeal against generic competitors including MSN Laboratories, Aurobindo, and Zydus Lifesciences, with one trial scheduled for November 2026 and another having secured favorable judgment on appeal.

The business operates with concentrated distribution risk. Four specialty pharmacy and specialty distributor customers account for approximately 79% of NUPLAZID product revenue and 44% of total product revenue as of December 31, 2025. DAYBUE faces even tighter concentration, sold in the U.S. through a single wholesale distributor with specialty pharmacy service. Supply chain geography introduces vulnerability: pimavanserin active pharmaceutical ingredient is manufactured by Siegfried AG in Switzerland, while trofinetide drug substance is manufactured by three suppliers in Italy. Competitive pressure comes from off-label use of lower-cost generic antipsychotics, multiple gene therapy companies developing Rett syndrome treatments, and larger competitors with greater R&D and manufacturing resources. NUPLAZID carries a boxed warning that may discourage prescribing, and the company explicitly identifies potential negative impact from publicly reported deaths of NUPLAZID patients as a disadvantage.

Near-term catalysts include DAYBUE STIX powder launch in Q1 2026, completion of remlifanserin Phase 2 RADIANT study enrollment in H1 2026, the European trofinetide reexamination outcome in Q3 2026, and ACP-711 Phase 2 essential tremor study initiation in Q4 2026. The company targets $1.0 billion in NUPLAZID net sales by 2028. In 2024, ACADIA completed a $28 million asset purchase from Saniona A/S and a $146.5 million asset sale to a third party.

Alamo Group Inc manufactures and sells specialized industrial and vegetation management equipment across two primary operating divisions. The Vegetation Management Division produces rotary, flail, disc, and finishing mowers, along with forestry and tree care products such as tree chippers, stump grinders, and mulchers. The Industrial Equipment Division operates a vocational truck business and manufactures excavators, vacuum trucks, street sweepers, snow removal equipment, and highway attenuator trucks. The company positions itself as a leader in high-quality, purpose-built equipment with one of the world's largest rotary mower manufacturing footprints and dominant positions in the European vegetation management market and U.S. governmental and agricultural segments. Operations span North America (United States and Canada) and Europe (United Kingdom, France, Netherlands) as primary markets, with secondary exposure to Brazil, Australia, the Middle East, North Africa, and Asia.

The company executed a CEO transition during the fiscal year. In the forward year, Alamo Group has initiated multiple operational consolidations and facility optimization actions: the Vegetation Management Division is installing new production lines and consolidating Rhino manufacturing into its Bush Hog facility in Selma, Alabama; the company completed the Ring-O-Matic, Inc. acquisition to expand its industrial vacuum excavation equipment portfolio; and it sold its Gibson City, Illinois facility as part of broader cost optimization. These moves suggest management is reshaping the footprint and production capacity in response to operational or market conditions. The company also disclosed pending product liability claims arising in the ordinary course of business, generally covered by insurance subject to self-insured retention amounts, though no quantified financial exposure was disclosed.

Alamo Group operates without material customer or supplier concentration—no single customer or supplier accounts for 10% or more of revenue or purchases. However, the company faces structural headwinds from several disadvantages it explicitly disclosed: some competitors possess substantially larger financial resources; the business depends heavily on the price and availability of raw materials and critical components like truck chassis and engines; supply chain disruptions pose real operational risk; and skilled labor shortages constrain capacity and retention. Engine emission regulations are tightening globally and could limit market access in key regions. Price competition remains the principal competitive lever, creating exposure to margin compression if the company cannot fully pass through input cost increases.

Alamo Group has undertaken a multi-year facility rationalization program, selling assets in Gibson City, Illinois (2025), Leavenworth Kansas, Kent Washington, and Quebec (2023), and consolidating multiple manufacturing operations into centralized locations during 2024. This restructuring reflects a shift toward operational efficiency and suggests management is right-sizing the production footprint against current demand conditions. Disclosure controls and internal control over financial reporting remain effective, and the auditor is KPMG LLP.

Capitol Federal positions itself as the leading originator of conventional one- to four-family loans in Kansas, leveraging a portfolio lending model, strong relationships with real estate agents, and a reputation for financial strength and customer service to compete against a broad array of adversaries including larger national and regional banks, credit unions, farm credit lenders, online lenders, and non-bank competitors.

No financial exposure has been quantified for the remanded litigation.

The company faces structural headwinds stemming from its business model and market position. Capitol Federal has disclosed that commercial loan portfolio growth increases credit risks, and the company faces exposure to downturns in regional housing and commercial real estate markets, longer holding periods for commercial collateral, and unpredictable commercial borrower cash flows.

Forward initiatives include implementing private banking products in fiscal 2026, launching digital onboarding for small business customers with risk management tools, deploying new technology for lockbox and accounts receivable services in calendar 2026, and rolling out digital banking enhancements for debit cardholders in the second quarter of fiscal 2026.
